narrative.t: Between 3 Sep 2026 and 2 Nov 2026 (NISAR, 6 passes, track 141 descending), the open water in the box (sea or a large lake running past the box edge) shrank from 1098 km² on 3 Sep to 1091 km² on 2 Nov, mostly between 15 Sep and 2 Nov (all water-dark pixels in the box: 1098 → 1091 km²).
narrative.s: Water-dark = smoothed brightness below 130 of 255 (valley after the darkest peak in the 3 Sep histogram); main body = largest connected dark patch, 1099 km² at its widest

narrative.t: On the map, 5.1 km² that was water-dark on 3 Sep no longer is by 2 Nov (orange, "water lost": drying shore), and 0.00 km² became water-dark (blue, "water gained").
narrative.s: NASA GIBS · NISAR GCOV display tiles, 3 Sep vs 2 Nov 2026; same water threshold, first vs last pass, only within 300 m of the dark water bodies

narrative.t: Across the whole box, 0.04 km² became much darker in radar (new water, wetter or smoother ground) and 0.16 km² became much brighter, 100% of it water-dark at the start, so mostly exposed shore.
narrative.s: NASA GIBS · NISAR GCOV display tiles, 3 Sep vs 2 Nov 2026; more than 4 robust σ (24 of 255 levels) after 5×5 smoothing; 0.25 km² on steep, shadowed terrain left out

narrative.t: The largest single patch (marker 1) is 0.32 km² of water lost, around 7.527° N, 80.858° W (brightness 109 → 134 of 255).
6.8 km² jumped by more than 4× its own normal pass-to-pass wobble, most of it (2.5 km²) between 3 Sep and 15 Sep; the same test on the first pair flags 11.6 km², a rough false-alarm level.
narrative.s: Per-pixel temporal anomaly over 6 passes (median absolute successive difference)

narrative.t: The plant signal (HV-like green channel) is about the same across the box (-1%).
Grouping pixels that behave alike over time gives 6 zones; none changes strongly as a whole, and the "dark all season" zone (likely open water) covers 71.2 km².
narrative.s: Unsupervised k-means on per-pixel time profiles; labels are interpretations

narrative.t: NASA EONET lists no natural events; USGS lists 115 M4+ earthquakes (largest M7.7) within about 50 km of this box in this period. That is context, not proof of cause.
narrative.s: NASA EONET v3 and USGS FDSN event APIs, box ± 0.5°
